tasks.notes:
SPLIT (2026-11-22, owner agreed): the generator code moved to #413; this ticket now holds only the builder steps (baseline full specs, rule-built builds, cost measurement, in-game verdict, findings). Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

Sequencing: this ticket follows #413 (non-builder spec generator), which must land first. If the trial needs changes to the builders themselves, land #407 (shared stoop/ground helpers) and #408 (feature_build split) first, so that code lands in the split modules.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes:

Owner: trees need more density. Performance evidence clarified 2026-11-21 (read-only): the trial quotes 962 s for 113 trees, but 8.5 s per tree is only an average of the reported total, not a measured per-tree bottleneck. The saved farmland trees-result.json (journal_seq 1292) records 17,915 positions, writer total 2.35 s, and 40.38 s summed across recorded apply stages; planning before site_kit.apply is not included in that result. The code already batches tree writes into one cell plan. The cause of the remainder of the reported command time is not established; profile planning and full command stages before choosing an optimisation or projecting dense-woodland cost. The earlier live-planning cache-thrash/low-probe-floor problem has a landed fix in #315 (planning from saved regions); distinguish it from the still-unexplained 962 s total. Numeric runtime limit remains to be agreed. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game. Profile 2026-11-21 (read-only dry run of trees_layer on 87,-48 under cProfile, current code with #315): 85 s total. planning_inputs 52.9 s, of which neighbour_owned 36 s (cell_journal._cell_owners rebuilds ownership per cell, uncacheable because builds are excluded; about 9 million block_id calls; scales with journal history, not tree count); dry site_kit.apply 16.9 s; surface warm-up 5.6 s; plan_cell (tree placement) 5.7 s. Dry run planted 51 trees and 10,306 blocks, not the trial's 113 trees and 17,915 positions, so it is indicative only. Current planning is about a minute, so the 962 s is not explained by planning on current code: it was pre-#315 live planning or the live apply stages (MCP write and readback), which a dry run cannot show. Next: time a live apply with the existing timed_stage output; the ownership lookup is a candidate optimisation. Live apply 2026-11-21 (87,-48, after prepare --apply cleared a stale readiness validation): 77 s wall, but NOT a clean redo and NOT the 113-tree workload. The apply did not undo the earlier trees pass (the dry run simulates that undo, apply_cell does not), so 51 crowns were skipped as trunk blocked and only 3 trees (556 blocks) were planted on top. Stages: layer planning 38.6 s, identity and readiness 4.1 s, journal begin 6.1 s, writer total 12.7 s (player hop 9.3 s), flush 3.6 s, readback 0.4 s. Side effect, owner chose not to repair: the trees mask for 87,-48 now holds 556 positions instead of the 17,915 of journal #1292, so the original trees remain in the world but are outside the mask (mask-based undo or redo would only touch the 3 new trees). A real full-workload timing needs undo then apply of the trees pass, on a cell where that is acceptable. Ghost frontier finding 2026-11-21 (ground apply on 46,-46, run from prepare then ground): the apply took 984 s and 883 s of it was the 'journal follow-ups' stage (registry.ensure writing 7 frontier ghost cells, journal #1656-1668, about 126 s and 1.1 million planned blocks per cell); every other stage summed to about 100 s. Still open: a full-workload trees timing needs an open-land cell with no planned features and a valid readiness check; 46,-46 is blocked by the planned houses_burgess_road feature (must land before trees/decor) and a stale validation (#232). Full-workload trees timing 2026-11-21 (46,-46 after the houses landed and a ground redo, frontier already complete so journal follow-ups took 0.003 s; existing planner, 256 crowns, 41,160 blocks, readback 0 mismatches): about 100 s of stage time. layer planning 54.2 s; registry.begin guard reads and journal write 14.0 s; surface warm-up in apply 9.8 s; readback 8.6 s; identity and readiness 3.9 s; flush 3.3 s; writer 2.6 s; backup 1.0 s. Placement is not the cost, and the trial 962 s is still unexplained (likely before #315 and #343, or a pending frontier). A runtime limit of a few minutes looks reachable; the numeric limit is still to be agreed. Dry-run cProfile of planning (inflated by the profiler): _box about 24 s, aerial tile decoding about 14 s, lidar about 7 s, neighbour_owned about 6.6 s, plan_cell about 6 s. Filed #345 for the box filter and decode caching; not filed: profiling registry.begin and the apply warm-up, and timing ground and decor. Owner feedback on the existing planner, filed as issue I-055 (held until #318): too sparse versus the aerial (dense wood with a few clearings), grass floor where podzol and ground cover belong, and no species variety. tasks.title: Railway line planner: pure function from lines and ground to a corridor plan (boxes, joins, gaps)
tasks.notes:
GOAL. A pure, deterministic function that turns railway evidence plus ground heights into a complete corridor plan: rails, powered rails, torches, ballast, slopes, planting, gaps and join records. It places nothing in a world.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md (all of it, especially "Method", "Game rules", "Owner decisions" 3 to 8 and 10); docs/plans/railway-prototype/ (rail_plan.py.txt is the working prototype of snapping, the level profile and the corridor; rail_power.py.txt is the powered-rail and torch rule; rail_apply.py.txt shows how plan columns became fills); the Line, point and span types from the railway evidence ticket (lib/sources/railway_evidence.py); lib/sources/lidar_heightmap.py (`terrain` is the DTM, `h` the surface, as block Y).

INPUTS: a Line (tracks as MC polylines); ground as arrays of block Y (`terrain`) and surface (`h`) for the area; the start cell; crossing and bridge/tunnel spans from the evidence ticket; optional incoming join records. OUTPUT (a plain JSON-able plan): `rails` [(x, y, z, shape, block)], `torches`, `columns` [(x, z, ground_y, surface_y, kind)] for bed and slopes, `planting`, `gaps` and `joins` (below), `failures` [{where, reason}].

DECISIONS YOU MUST HONOUR (owner, 2026-11-22):
- Rails: snap each track to a 4-connected cell path (the prototype's method: 0.25-block densify, corner cell nearer the line, remove loops and backtracks). An ascending rail is allowed only where the cell and both neighbours are collinear. Steps are 1 block, at least RAIL_MIN_STEP_RUN cells apart (a config constant, default 100; no further research on the figure). Paired tracks use a shared target so they stay within one level. Tracks of a Line start at one shared level, or at the level given by an incoming join record.
- POWERED RAIL: every straight cell, ascending included, is `powered_rail[shape=...,powered=true]` with a `redstone_torch` two blocks below the rail (air, rail, ground, torch). Corner cells stay plain `rail` (powered rail cannot turn). The torch's own support block must be solid, else report a failure.
- Corridor: gravel bed within 2.3 blocks of any track cell; grass side slopes at 2 blocks across per 1 block of height, out to 40 blocks, meeting the ground. The feature trumps roads: where a road crosses, the plan's ground in the footprint uses the road surface from the vector map (lib/sources/ground_sources.py) instead of grass.
- PLANTING (part of the line feature): where the surface model is above the ground model inside the footprint, place bushes with gaps in the grass; elsewhere grass; never tall trees (clearance).
- SIZE: the plan covers a 2048 x 2048 MC box around the start cell. A line leaving the box is cut where it leaves, and the plan records a JOIN (cell, level, direction, tracks) at the cut so the next feature can start at that level. Simple box maths; no track-length counting.
- GAPS: at each level crossing, bridge or tunnel span the profile runs straight through (levels continuous, no step inside) but the plan builds nothing there and records a GAP with the level, direction and tracks at both ends. For a crossing the span is the road width plus 1 block each side (road width from ground_sources.road_width).
- BEST EFFORT, FAIL LOUDLY: where a stretch cannot be made rail-legal, add a clear entry to `failures` (cell, what, why) instead of improvising. Failures to detect: a path that is not 4-connected after repair; ground data missing under a track cell; a level that must deviate from the ground by more than RAIL_MAX_DEVIATION (config, default 8); an unsolvable join level. Junctions and sidings are never planned here (human work).

ACCEPTANCE (synthetic ground only; suggest lib/builds/railway_plan.py with lib/builds/test_railway_plan.py; run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_railway_plan`): a `validate_plan(plan)` helper that every test also calls, asserting each consecutive cell pair is 4-adjacent, no cell is revisited, every rail shape connects both neighbours, every ascending rail rises exactly one toward its next cell on a collinear run, every straight cell is powered with a torch at y-2, no corner is powered, and no step is closer than RAIL_MIN_STEP_RUN. Cases: flat straight line; a 45-degree diagonal (all corners, so no step possible and the profile must still be valid); a quarter-circle curve; a slope needing three steps; a double-track pair staying within one level; a 3000-block synthetic line splitting at the 2048 box into two plans whose join levels match; a crossing mid-run producing a gap with end records and a continuous level; missing ground producing a `failures` entry and no exception. Optionally add a recorded-terrain regression if you can commit a small excerpt, but synthetic ground is required.

DO NOT: call any MCP tool, touch the live world, write the journal, or add a new block-placement path (the integration ticket does that). Keep the function pure.
WORKFLOW: task/* branch, ship-branch skill. builderTask false. This changes planner geometry, so treat it as a stretch under docs/agents/model-and-effort.md: ask the owner before raising model or effort.

ADDED 2026-11-22 (owner): RAILS UNDER A BRIDGE. A road or path bridge over the line (see the evidence ticket's overhead spans) is NOT a gap: the rails and bed run straight under it at ground level. But the planting rule (surface model above ground model means bush) would read the bridge deck as vegetation. EXCLUDE every overhead-span deck column (and any column the lidar marks as kind 4 "structure") from planting, and from slope and bed adjustment where the deck's supports are; keep a clearance of at least 5 blocks above the rail under a deck, and report a failure if the ground profile would leave less than that (for example an embankment that rises into a deck). Add synthetic tests: a deck over two tracks produces no bushes and no gap under it; a profile that would rise into the deck is a failure.

Shared seams (housekeeping review, docs/plans/housekeeping-review.md): use cellmath for cell and neighbour maths and add no private block, cell or tag tables.

tasks.title: Railway line feature integration: cell workflow skips, ownership, backup, undo
tasks.notes:
GOAL. Make the railway line a real, journalled FEATURE in the normal cell workflow: skip fast when there is nothing to do, build from the planner's plan with a structure backup, own its footprint so later passes leave it alone, and undo cleanly.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 2, 3, 5 to 8, 10, and "Not in the normal workflow yet"); GLOSSARY.md (Element, Feature); rules/handoff-layered-passes.md (sections 1, 3, 4 and 11: pass order, masks, undo, cross-cell effects); rules/feature-builds.md; lib/journal/cell_features.py and lib/journal/cell_journal.py (how a feature and its footprint are recorded); scripts/cell_registry.py (`propose_feature_candidates`, readiness); lib/site/site_kit.py (`apply`, `_structure_backup`, structure backups, readback); lib/site/element_undo.py; lib/builds/feature_build.py (how a feature spec in site/builds/<name>.json works); the planner (lib/builds/railway_plan.py) and evidence (lib/sources/railway_evidence.py) modules; docs/plans/railway-prototype/rail_apply.py.txt and rail_verify.py.txt.

DECISIONS YOU MUST HONOUR (owner, 2026-11-22):
- PER-CELL WORKFLOW: a cell with no railway is skipped at once. A cell already covered by an earlier railway feature is skipped at once ("marked already by a nearby cell that was done first"). Otherwise plan a railway feature starting from that cell, 2048 x 2048 box, join records at box cuts.
- The feature OWNS its whole footprint: rails, ballast, slopes, planting. The cell trees and decor passes never place inside it (the rules already say a major feature wins; check this holds for railway footprints and enforce it if not), and the ground layer yields to it. Where a road crosses, the feature lays the road surface itself.
- The feature's gaps (crossings, bridges, tunnels) and joins are recorded in the feature record so the crossing-feature ticket can read them.
- BEST EFFORT, FAIL LOUDLY: if the plan has any `failures`, stop BEFORE any block is written and print them. A human fixes those bits.
- Powered rail with a torch two blocks below, corners plain, junctions untouched.

BUILD:
1. Feature proposal for railway in the per-cell flow (propose, prepare, readiness), with the two instant skips.
2. A spec in site/builds/ (name `railway_<tx>_<tz>`) that points at the plan or embeds it, validated by the registry check.
3. Apply through site_kit.apply: structure backup tiles, fills and rail writes, journalled ownership of every footprint column, and a READ-BACK that rescans what was written and RETRIES misses. The trial's first powered-rail pass missed 45 cells (39 rails, 6 torches) near MC x 7376 to 7414 and a retry fixed them; the cause was never found, so treat a miss as normal and retry, then fail loudly if it persists.
4. Undo through the existing element undo, restoring the structure backup and clearing the journal ownership. Covered-cell marking must be undone too.
5. Docs: a railway section in rules/feature-builds.md; GLOSSARY.md note that a railway line is a feature, not a layer.

ACCEPTANCE (tests with MemoryBlocks and the journal test kit, no live server; run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <your test stems>`): proposing for a cell with no railway returns nothing; proposing for a cell covered by an existing railway feature returns nothing; a planned feature applies into MemoryBlocks and the journal shows ownership of every footprint column; a later trees or decor pass over the cell writes nothing inside the footprint; read-back detects a deliberately dropped block and the retry restores it; a persistent miss fails loudly; a plan with failures writes no block at all; undo restores MemoryBlocks exactly; two features on adjacent boxes carry matching join records.

DO NOT: apply to the live world, run a real-place build, or design crossings/bridges/tunnels (their own tickets). If you want a live smoke test, stop and leave it to the real-stretch trial ticket.
WORKFLOW: task/* branch, ship-branch skill. builderTask false. This changes journal ownership across layers, so it is a stretch under docs/agents/model-and-effort.md: ask the owner before raising model or effort.

Shared seams (housekeeping review, docs/plans/housekeeping-review.md): use cellmath, the shared builder helpers (#407) and world-provider roles (#393) rather than new private tables or imports.

tasks.title: Crossing feature mechanism: spec, join records, not-ready gate and crossing builder
tasks.notes:
GOAL. The shared mechanism for crossing, bridge and tunnel features: a spec format, the join records that tie them to railway line features, the "not ready" gate, and a builder for a level crossing driven by a spec. Claude designs each crossing from evidence in a later ticket; this ticket makes that possible.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 7, 9, 10, 11); docs/plans/bridges-and-tunnels.md ("Already decided"); lib/builds/feature_build.py (feature spec pattern in site/builds/<name>.json); lib/blocks/block_reference.py (block id validation); lib/journal/cell_features.py; the line feature module from the integration ticket (its gap and join records); lib/sources/ground_sources.py (road width and surface kinds).

DECISIONS YOU MUST HONOUR (owner, 2026-11-22):
- Each level crossing, bridge and tunnel is its own FEATURE and MAY include rail lines. It records which abutting railway features it joins (cell, level, direction, tracks).
- It is built AFTER the line features and REFUSES ("not ready", exit non-zero, nothing written) until both abutting line features exist in the journal. The line features leave a gap and write end records; this builder reads them.
- The rail feature trumps the road: at a level crossing this feature lays the road surface across the rails itself, using road data, and the rails through at the recorded level (straight cells powered with a torch two blocks below, as in the line feature).
- Gates, lights and bell exist only where the spec says, and the spec's flags come from the OSM tags (`crossing:barrier`, `crossing:light`, `crossing:bell`). Their style and colours are chosen by Claude from Street View in the crossing's own build (a later ticket), so the spec must carry free block ids for bars, posts and lamps, validated against block_reference.py, plus a field for the evidence references (frame ids).
- No default-style fallback and no separate survey: a crossing with no spec is not built.

BUILD:
1. Spec schema (JSON in site/builds/, name `crossing_<tx>_<tz>_<n>`): kind (crossing now; bridge and tunnel only reserve the header), abutting line feature ids and join records, road way ids and surface, rail tracks, barrier/light/bell flags with block ids and positions, evidence references. Document the schema in the module docstring and rules/feature-builds.md. Validate it in the registry check (registry_verify.check_feature_specs).
2. The "not ready" gate and the join-record reader.
3. The crossing builder: road surface across, rails at the join level (reuse the line feature's rail and powered-rail rules, do not copy them), barriers, lights, bell marker; journalled ownership of its footprint; structure backup; read-back with retry; undo.
4. Bridge and tunnel: only the shared header, join reading and gate. Their geometry waits for the bridge and tunnel decisions ticket.

ACCEPTANCE (MemoryBlocks, synthetic specs; no live server): a valid crossing spec builds into MemoryBlocks with rails continuous across the road at the recorded level; with both neighbours missing or only one present the builder refuses and writes nothing; a spec whose block id is not a valid block is rejected; a spec with no barrier flag builds no gates; flags that disagree with the OSM tags recorded in the spec's evidence are rejected; undo restores MemoryBlocks exactly; the registry check reports a malformed spec.

DO NOT: choose real colours or styles (the Claude crossing ticket does), build a real crossing, apply to the live world, or implement bridge or tunnel geometry.
WORKFLOW: task/* branch, ship-branch skill. builderTask false.

Shared seams (housekeeping review, docs/plans/housekeeping-review.md): use cellmath and the barrier vocabulary module (#398) rather than new private tables.

tasks.title: Railway trial D: build the trial corridor with the production line feature, ride it, judge it
tasks.notes:
GOAL. First real use of the production railway line feature: build the trial corridor in the live world, ride it end to end, and judge it with the owner. This is the representative build and the in-game judgement the code tickets cannot do.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md (all of it: what the 2026-11-22 trial found, "Owner decisions", "Ticket plan"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask dispatch gate; the owner must be present); rules/build-roles.md and `python3 scripts/build_roles.py --world southampton-build show`; rules/process.md; the railway line feature (lib/builds/railway_plan.py and the integration module) and its README or rules section.

PLACE: the trial corridor in world southampton-build, MC x 6740 to 7430, z -4400 to -3890 (cells 52..58, -35..-31). Ghost ground already exists for all of it. It contains one double-track main line, one double-track branch curve, one level crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34), two mapped rail bridge spans (near 7285,-4290 and from 7415,-4107 to 7474,-4020), and 19 rail switches (a junction near 6820,-4085). The 2026-11-22 trial corridor was removed; the area is back to ghost ground.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: docs/plans/railway.md "Owner decisions" 1 to 14. In particular: powered rail on every straight cell with a torch two blocks below; junctions, sidings and yards are NOT built (leave gaps for humans and report them); the line leaves gaps at the crossing and both bridges with end records (the crossing feature is built later by its own ticket); best effort, and fail loudly where a stretch cannot be made rail-legal.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and the build roles; start under `python3 scripts/site_lock.py --world southampton-build run <owner> "<task>" -- <cmd>`. Plan with the production builder; read its failures list first. Dry-run before applying.
2. Apply, then verify by read-back (rails match the plan, every powered rail powered, torches present).
3. With the owner in the game, ride a cart end to end on each track; record where it stops or derails and why. Check corners, ascending rails, the speed on staircase stretches, the bed and slopes against the real surroundings, and the planting.
4. List the spots a human should fix (junction, the gaps at the crossing and bridges, anything that looked wrong), with coordinates. File any snags in the world repo (scripts/issues.py, the snag skill), not as tasks.
5. Write the findings into docs/plans/railway.md under a "Trial D" heading: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the footprint (should be none), minutes and session tokens used (state the method), actual models and efforts, the ride result, and the owner's in-game verdict.
6. NEXT STEP, DO NOT FILE IT YET: decor sidings, yards and spurs (best-effort decor, clean unbroken runs only, never tied into junctions). The owner chose the study area: the yard around 50.91436,-1.45871 (MC 1901,-3299, cell 23,-32; 17 sidings, 3 crossovers, 2 spurs, 20 switches, a viaduct over the rails; probe extracts in the world repo under reference/vector_map/rail_probe_complex/). Say in the findings whether the line is good enough to start it and what its brief should contain.

ACCEPTANCE: docs/plans/railway.md has a Trial D section with a Cost heading and table rows and the owner's in-game verdict; the ride result per track is recorded; the human-fix list has coordinates; nothing written outside the footprint.

tasks.title: First crossing feature: the level crossing near 6980,-4343 from OSM tags and Street View
tasks.notes:
GOAL. Design and build the first level crossing feature, in game, with the owner: the crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34). Claude chooses the gates, lights and colours from OSM tags and Street View, then builds it using the crossing mechanism.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 7, 9, 10, 11); docs/plans/bridges-and-tunnels.md ("Already decided"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask gate; owner present); the crossing feature module and schema from the crossing mechanism ticket (lib/builds/, rules/feature-builds.md); the `snag` skill; rules/build-roles.md.

EVIDENCE ALREADY FOUND (OSM, node on each of the two tracks about 4 blocks apart, near 50.92340 N, 1.38633 W): `railway=level_crossing`, `crossing:barrier=double_half`, `crossing:light=yes`, `crossing:bell=yes`, `crossing:activation=remote`, description "Manually Controlled Barriers monitored with Closed-Circuit Television (MCB-CCTV)". The branch line crosses a road here; read the road data for the surface and width.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: the rail feature trumps the road; the crossing feature lays the road surface across the rails itself; gates, lights and bell exist only because the OSM tags say so (barrier double_half, light yes, bell yes); their STYLE and COLOURS come from Street View, chosen in this build, with the frame ids recorded as evidence; no default style and no separate survey. The crossing is built after both abutting line features exist and joins their recorded levels.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and that the line features either side of the gap exist (the real-stretch trial ticket builds them). If not, stop and report; do not build the line here.
2. Get Street View frames: `python3 shims/streetview_sample.py --world southampton-build sample --cell 54,-34` (optional `--grid` and `--yaws`; it has no dry-run flag, so before running it tell the owner the source (Google Street View thumbnails), the cell, the number of frames and that they save under instance/streetview/, and wait for a yes; see config/system-providers.json for the licence note: do not commit the frames). Read the sheet. Note the barrier arms, lamps, signs, colours, and anything the OSM tags missed.
3. Record the evidence with scripts/decision_record.py (`evidence add`, `phase add`), write the crossing spec in site/builds/, choose valid block ids for bars, posts and lamps (iron bars and the other colour variants available in this game version; check lib/blocks/block_reference.py), dry-run, apply under the site lock, read back.
4. Judge it in game with the owner: does it read as that crossing, are the colours right, does a cart pass through. Fix by editing the spec and re-applying; file snags in the world repo, not as tasks.
5. Add a short Crossing section to docs/plans/railway.md: what Street View showed, choices made and why, what looked right or wrong, cost (minutes, session tokens, method), and the owner's verdict. Say whether the same approach should be repeated for other crossings.

ACCEPTANCE: the crossing spec and its evidence record exist in the world repo; the crossing is built, read back and judged in game by the owner; the railway findings file has the Crossing section with a Cost heading and the owner's verdict.

tasks.title: Find what triggers Minecraft rate-limit waits during applies
tasks.notes: From the 2026-11-21 B35 rebuild thread. The same plan applied four times: fill stage took 122 s with 1 rate-limit retry, 605 s with 10, 485 s with 7, 125 s with 0 (each retry is a fixed 'Minecraft rate limit: retrying in 60s' wait). Unknown what triggers it. One unverified guess: other Minecraft MCP calls (teleport, scan, capture) from a parallel session while an apply runs. Spike: log request timestamps and the server's limit response during an apply, run once with no other calls and once with background calls, and record the limit, whether it is per second or per window, and whether the writer's pacing (see McpWriter, the paced MCP interval in rules/slow-commands.md) can stay under it. Output: a short finding in docs/ with numbers, and either a tuned pacing constant or a filed fix. Acceptance: the finding states the limit and the cause with measurements.

tasks.title: Stairs: shape every stair against all neighbouring stairs, any material (all stair writers)
tasks.notes:
Owner requirement (2026-11-22, #358 review of the pitched Burgess Road roofs): a stair's presentation depends on neighbouring stairs on the same level. A stair rotated 90 degrees directly in front of or behind another stair turns it into an outer or inner corner. This must be baked into every part of the code that places stairs so the result is smooth. Any stair can change any other: material does not matter (unlike fences), only same Y, same half and facing.

What exists (read-only check): roof_geometry.stair_shape_from_neighbours is material-agnostic and matches vanilla getStairsShape. house_build.roof applies it only among that roof's own stairs (cells in `facings` at the same Y), roof_lint.stair_shape_mismatches checks the planned cells, and the 0.75 Burgess Road plan reported 0 mismatches and 0 readback mismatches. Stairs written elsewhere carry no shape and do not look at neighbours: stoop.stair uses (door steps, ledge stair, the raised-door inner stair), the interior spruce stairs in house_build.doors, and any other builder or layer that writes `_stairs[` states. Stairs from neighbouring plans, other builds or the live world at the same Y are not consulted by the roof pass. The owner's in-game view of the rebuilt roofs still looks patchy at stair joins (cause not yet established; needs the live block states under the crosshair compared with the plan).

Scope: (1) one shared helper, working over the final plan cells plus a live-world reader, that resolves the shape of every stair against every stair neighbour at the same Y and half, any material, in both directions (plan wins over live for cells the plan writes), and is the only way stairs get their shape; (2) use it as a last pass in house_build, feature_build, stoop and any other stair writer, so a stair next to an earlier build's stair or a stoop stair is shaped too, and report cells where a neighbour stair outside the plan would change a planned stair's shape; (3) extend roof_lint to compare plan against live read-back after apply for shape, not just plan against plan; (4) find the cause of the patchy joins in the rebuilt Burgess Road roofs by comparing live states with the plan, and fix facing choices if the shape rule is not the cause.

Not in scope: the world rebuild and the I-056 S-103 verdict, which stay with #358.
